objective: Close the standalone mapper replay ambiguity by composing the counted M117 descriptor scheduler directly with the M120 three-beat tail-bypass mapper and signed19 lane accumulator, then verify end-to-end token and numeric conservation in commercial VCS.

motivation.m119_open_p0: A standalone ready/valid mapper correctly accepts the same payload again when it is presented as a second legal transaction; deduplication belongs to the sequence-owning scheduler.
motivation.closure_scope: The scheduler owns service progress and directly drives the numeric island, so a service token is consumed once at the single composed handshake cut in the directed descriptor run.

architecture.composed_accept_contract: scheduler service_accept and numeric service_accept must equal service_valid && service_ready every cycle
architecture.fault_policy: scheduler and numeric protocol failures are sticky and combined fail-closed

paper_safe_statement: Commercial VCS verifies a directed scheduler-to-numeric PWP service island. Two dense W384 descriptors produce 99072 counted service tokens; all 98304 scheduled event tokens produce exactly 98304 signed19 accumulator writes, while 256 three-beat synchronous 256-bit weight fetches use tail bypass without a per-key bubble. This closes the standalone mapper ownership ambiguity only for the directed integrated sequence; heldout traces, foundry SRAM, physical speedup and system speedup remain unadmitted.
prohibited_claims: Do not call the directed two-descriptor run a heldout duplicate, retry or escape replay proof.
Do not call behavioral weight or lane memories foundry SRAM macros.
Do not infer macro area, energy or timing from logical bytes or VCS.
Do not promote the 2.53546204172554x module cycle projection to RTL-measured, physical, system or headline speedup.
